01

Resolution/what WGS measures

vSNP3 compares every base in the genome.

vSNP3 aligns reads to a reference genome and counts every difference, reporting the number of SNPs between any two isolates. Methods that read only a few loci, such as spoligotyping and MLST, assign isolates to a single type; comparing the whole genome separates isolates within that type and measures how far apart they are.

Overview/the whole process

The whole process on one page.

Reads in, aligned to a reference, one VCF per sample collecting in a database that only grows — then split into groups, each read as a tree and a SNP table.

vSNP3 · Kapur Lab · Penn State · USDA
03

The database/reference types

The database is organized by reference type.

A reference type is one folder per reference genome, holding everything needed to compare samples against it — together with every VCF already processed there.

Mycobacterium_AF2122/ ├── *.fasta the reference genome ├── *.gbk annotation → a SNP gets a gene ├── *_define_filter.xlsx defining SNPs + per-group filters ├── *_metadata.xlsx file stem → display label └── *_remove_from_analysis.xlsx samples/regions to drop
  • Add an organism by adding a folder. The reference name is the folder name.
  • The VCF set only grows as samples are processed against that reference.
  • The reference defines the positions. Two samples called against the same reference can be compared position by position. Against a different reference the same site carries a different number, so Step 2 will not mix them.

Each reference type is its own database — separate Step 1, Step 2 and comparisons

  • Mycobacterium_H37step 1 sample1, sample2 … step 2 comparisons
  • Mycobacterium_AF2122step 1 sample1, sample2 … step 2 comparisons
  • mtbc0_v1.1step 1 sample1, sample2 … step 2 comparisons
  • Brucella_abortus1step 1 sample1, sample2 … step 2 comparisons
  • …one folder per reference, added as needed
vSNP3 · Kapur Lab · Penn State · USDA
04

Step 1/per sample

Step 1 aligns one sample’s reads to a reference and calls its variants.

Reads go in; every difference from the reference is called and every uncovered region is recorded. This is the slow stage, and it runs once per sample.

  • Zero coverage is recorded. A - later means no data at that position, not a match.
  • The BAM is kept, so the reads behind any call can be reviewed later.
  • Adding samples is incremental. Alignment is done once.

In bdtools: pick the reference, Grab ready-to-run samples, then Runbdtools · vSNP GUI v0.4.80 · Step 1.

05

Quality control/between Step 1 and Step 2

Review the Step 1 statistics before running Step 2.

Step 1 flags each sample PASS or REVIEWbdtools · vSNP GUI v0.4.80 · Step 1 Results with the reason. Failing samples are excluded before a comparison runs.

MetricHealthyReview when
Average depth of coverage≥ 40×< 20×
Reads mapping to the reference> 90%< 80%
% reference with zero coverage< 5%> 10%
R1/R2 % passing Q20> 50%very low
Quality SNP countorganism-typicala spike

Low mapping usually means contaminating reads — host DNA or another organism. Parse the sample down to your target taxon with Kraken from inside Step 1, then re-run it.

06

Large sample sets/defining SNPs

Defining SNPs sort samples into groups before the comparison is run.

Defining SNPs assign each sample to a group, so every table you actually read is smaller and internally comparable. A whole-complex table is thousands of positions across dozens of samples, and the differences between lineages drown out the few SNPs that separate recent cases.

Adding a group is adding a name and a position to that file — the next run reports it as its own group. A real run of this MTBC set produced 173 groups, each with its own table, tree, and SNP distances.

vSNP3 · Kapur Lab · Penn State · USDA
07

Step 2/comparison

Each Step 1 result joins the database; Step 2 compares any selection from it.

Every finished sample is copied into the project’s VCF database, which only ever grows. Step 2 takes whichever samples you tick, splits them into groups, and builds a table and tree for each one. No reads are re-aligned.

  • You tick what goes in: this project’s samples plus optional shared panels. See the builderbdtools · vSNP GUI v0.4.80 · Step 2 build
  • One table and tree per subgroup come out of the same run. See the outputsbdtools · vSNP GUI v0.4.80 · Step 2 Results
vSNP3 · Kapur Lab · Penn State · USDA
08

Reading the output/table and tree together

The SNP table and the tree show the same data two ways.

Same samples, same SNPs, presented two ways: the tablebdtools · vSNP GUI v0.4.80 · cascade table lists them position by position, the tree draws the same differences as distance. A block of shared SNPs in the table is the branch that groups those samples in the tree. In the built-in tree viewerbdtools · vSNP GUI v0.4.80 · tree viewer, clicking a clade opens the table for just those samples.

vSNP3 · Kapur Lab · Penn State · USDA
09

Validation/the v in vSNP

vSNP stands for validate SNP: any call can be checked in the read alignment.

In bdtools a cell in the cascading table is a linkbdtools · vSNP GUI v0.4.80 · cascade table: clicking it opens the alignment at that position. When two isolates differ by only a few SNPs, each position affects the result, so they are reviewed in the read alignmentbdtools · IGV · MTBC0:1,263,022 rather than taken from the table alone.

vSNP3 · Kapur Lab · Penn State · USDA
10

Summary/six properties

Six properties of the vSNP3 workflow.

What the preceding slides add up to.

01

Zero coverage is recorded

A gap is reported as missing data, never as agreement with the reference.

02

Step 1 and Step 2 are separate

Align once per sample; compare as often as you like.

03

One reference per dataset

Positions stay comparable. References are never mixed.

04

Grouping is yours to maintain

Defining SNPs are a curated file, not a clustering threshold.

05

Sample differences are visually validated

A table cell opens the read alignment at that position.

06

Every run is repeatable

Inputs, parameters and versions are stored with every run.

In bdtools every step above is a button, with the same layout as the other tools in the suite. The command line is optional.

Running it/five steps

Running vSNP3 in bdtools: five steps.

All of it in the browser. Allow about an hour, most of it unattended while Step 1 aligns.

  1. 01Open the dashboard and launch vSNP3bdtools · dashboard. Check the paths in Settings.
  2. 02Create a project and add inputsbdtools · vSNP GUI v0.4.80 · Projects & Inputs — server files, drag-and-drop, or SRA accessions.
  3. 03Step 1: choose the reference, then Runbdtools · vSNP GUI v0.4.80 · Step 1. This is the longest stage.
  4. 04Review Step 1 Resultsbdtools · vSNP GUI v0.4.80 · Step 1 Results. Exclude anything flagged REVIEW.
  5. 05Step 2: tick what to compare, then Runbdtools · vSNP GUI v0.4.80 · Step 2 Results. Read the table and tree together.

Practice data. docs/TRAINING.md Module 4 runs the whole workflow on nine public TB accessions; Module 5 scales it to a labelled MTBC panel. docs/TRAINING.html is the same guide as one standalone file you can email or hand out.
